findings: The cycle lens measures six primary steps only and excludes process startup, construction, counterfactual branch cloning, checkpoints, replay steps, compact evidence, JSON, and the Rust test harness.
Five warm measurements used 563225024 to 576193339 bare-organism cycles, with a median of 564658829 cycles and 130720151 CPU nanoseconds for all six primary steps.
The median bare cost is about 94109805 cycles and 21786692 CPU nanoseconds per physical body step on this Apple M5 Pro.

Of the median bare cost, the core body used about 503838452 cycles across six steps and the sensorimotor adapter used about 63738251 cycles; separately reported medians do not necessarily sum to the median total.
An independent run measured 578498651 bare cycles and 134144110 CPU nanoseconds, within the retained warm range.
The observed and unobserved paths produce exactly equal next harnesses, observations, canonical checkpoints, return phases, physical work, and natural quiescence.
Host counters remain outside body input, state, physical time, checkpoint, fingerprint, replay predicates, and scientific evidence.
The unchanged complete proof fixture still passes in 0.28 seconds, and the representative workstation regression suite passes in 0.21 seconds.
residual_uncertainty: These are host CPU counters for this Apple M5 Pro and macOS version; other processors and thermal states will differ.

The body-core phase is directly bracketed. Sensorimotor-adapter cost is the remaining transition cost after subtracting counter reads, transaction clone, diagnostic projection, fingerprinting, and core-body phases.
The measurement answers implementation cost for six primary transitions; it is not capability evidence, research authority, or a claim about the future 64/64 run.
